# housecall-pro-mcp

> Open-source MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Housecall Pro. Connects
> Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible AI agent to a Housecall Pro
> account: customers, jobs, job appointments, checklists, invoices and their
> customer-facing documents, estimates, price book, employees, tags, revenue
> summaries, CSV exports, and the account's working hours and bookable slots,
> plus writes (create customers, service addresses, jobs, line items, estimates
> and leads; book, move and undo appointments; dispatch a crew to a job; change
> several of a job's line items at once; record an estimate option as approved
> or declined; tag jobs; maintain the price book) that follow the API key's own
> access level.

For: Housecall Pro business owners and developers connecting an AI assistant
to their field-service data.

Independent open-source project by HCP API. Not affiliated with,
endorsed by, or sponsored by Housecall Pro.

## Key facts
- Install: `npx housecall-pro-mcp`, no build step, Node 18+
- Auth: `HCP_API_KEY` environment variable
- Housecall Pro API access requires their MAX plan, and only an admin user can
  generate a key (My Apps, Go to App store, API Key Management)
- A key cannot be edited once created, only copied or deleted
- Read-only vs full-access is chosen when the key is generated, and this
  server follows it
- Money is handled in dollars in both directions
- No tool sends an email, a text or an estimate on your behalf. Booking a
  visit, moving one and undoing a booking send the customer nothing themselves;
  Housecall Pro still sends its own appointment reminders nearer the date, per
  your account settings. Automations set up inside Housecall Pro run on their
  own, outside this server's control
- Booking is one call: creating an appointment on a job also sets that job's
  schedule, so the work is scheduled and dispatched together. Every appointment
  needs at least one technician
- `hcp_dispatch_job` puts a crew on a job's work. That route is customer-visible:
  Housecall Pro may tell the customer who is coming, and what it sends has not
  been watched either way, so treat it as reaching them
- `hcp_approve_estimate_options` and `hcp_decline_estimate_options` record the
  customer's answer on one or more options, in Housecall Pro's own terms: pro
  approved and pro declined, the shop writing down an answer rather than a
  request going out to ask for one. Doing it emailed and texted nobody when it
  was exercised, which is not a promise for another account - Housecall Pro's
  automations and notification settings send on their own
- `hcp_contactability` unions every do-not-contact signal a customer record
  exposes - notifications switched off, a do-not-contact tag, do-not-contact
  language in the notes - and names the one it cannot: Housecall Pro's Do Not
  Service checkbox is a dashboard setting this integration cannot read. A
  `contactable: true` therefore means no signal was found on the readable
  surface, not a clearance to contact
- `hcp_update_job_line_items` changes several of a job's line items in one
  request, where `hcp_update_job_line_item` is one request per row
- An arrival window must be a width Housecall Pro accepts: 0, 15, 20, 60, 120,
  180 or 240 minutes, where 0 means an exact time
- A booking can be undone, but the API has no route that deletes a job, and a
  customer service address cannot be changed or removed once added
- Appointments belong to a job and there is no account-wide appointment list,
  though the account's own working hours and bookable slots do read account wide
- Shop defaults (job duration, arrival window, starting line item) are kept in a
  file the installed server owns, per machine rather than per Housecall Pro
  account, and nothing in that file is sent to Housecall Pro

- The tool surface is selectable. `--read-only` (or `HCP_READ_ONLY=1`) registers
  no tool that can change anything, which is independent of the key's own access
  level: the write tools are absent rather than merely refused. `--toolsets=a,b`
  (or `HCP_TOOLSETS`) registers only named groups, out of company, customers,
  jobs, estimates, invoices, pricebook, schedule, reports and admin, plus `all`
  and `default`. `admin` (registry maintenance writes) is not in the default
  set; listing tags and job types is, because interpreting job data needs the
  registries. A misspelled group name stops the server rather than starting it
  with tools missing
- Without HCP_API_KEY the server starts keyless: only hcp_render_report and
  hcp_api_notes register, and nothing can reach a Housecall Pro account. The
  renderer works on findings from any source, including dashboard CSV exports
- Every tool carries the MCP spec's annotations, so a client can tell a read
  from a write, a write from a delete, and either from something that reaches the
  customer, without inferring it from the name
- `hcp_api_notes` answers what the Housecall Pro API actually does for a given
  topic where that differs from its published documentation: 12 documented routes
  that do not exist, writes that are accepted and silently ignored, and fields
  whose units are not what they look like. It reads a table compiled into the
  server and makes no API request. The same tables are exposed as MCP resources
  at `hcp://api-notes/quirks` and `hcp://api-notes/phantom-routes`
- Never trust a 2xx on a Housecall Pro write. Several routes answer 200 without
  changing anything. Tagging a job and untagging one read the job back after
  writing and report whether the change is actually visible, including reporting
  it as unknown rather than guessing when the record cannot settle it
